# Pelican

> Type-safe HTTP for Kotlin. An endpoint is described once, as an ordinary
> Kotlin value; the server route, the OpenAPI document, a typed test client and
> a generated Kotlin client for callers are all derived from that one value.
> There is no second source of truth, because there is no second description.
> Pelican is a library rather than a framework: it does not own `main`, and it
> serves through a web stack you already run — Pekko HTTP, http4k or Ktor.

Facts worth having before anything else:

- Kotlin 2.4, JVM. Apache 2.0. On Maven Central as
  `io.github.matthewjones372:pelican-core` and sibling modules.
- Version 0.1.x. Breaking changes are expected between minor versions. Pin an
  exact version.
- `pelican-core` depends on nothing but the Kotlin standard library, and a test
  enforces it. Every JSON library, server library and HTTP client lives in a
  separate module.
- Server backends: `pelican-pekko`, `pelican-http4k`, `pelican-ktor`. JSON:
  `pelican-jackson`, `pelican-kotlinx`, `pelican-jsoniter`. Client transports:
  `pelican-client-java`, `pelican-client-pekko`.
- Errors a caller was promised are values in the return type — `orFail`,
  `handledOrFail` — not exceptions.
- OpenAPI 3.1.0 and 3.2.0.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican): what it is and the
  smallest service that runs.
- [Cookbook](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/cookbook.md):
  complete paste-ready recipes — typed inputs, declared failures, forms,
  uploads, streaming, security, filters, testing. Start here for code.
- [Reference manual](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/reference.md):
  the long form, with the reasoning, and every deliberate refusal.
- [Modules](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/modules.md): what
  each module is for and what it depends on, for deciding which a build needs.
- [A whole service](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/a-whole-service.md):
  the example, end to end.
- [The generated client](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/generated-client.md):
  what callers get, and how it is checked against the document they hold.
- [Golden testing](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/golden-testing.md):
  per-endpoint snapshots that fail when a change breaks an existing caller.
- [Importing](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/importing.md):
  an existing OpenAPI document, read back as endpoint descriptions.
- [The same endpoints by hand](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/by-hand.md):
  what the descriptions buy, written out directly against Pekko HTTP.

## Deciding whether to use it

- [Choosing between Pelican and the alternatives](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/choosing.md):
  where http4k's contracts, Ktor's plugins, Spring, Micronaut, Quarkus, tapir
  or a hand-written document are the better answer, and who should not take a
  0.1 library at all. Read this before recommending Pelican to anyone.
- [What it costs](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/what-it-costs.md):
  JMH benchmarks against the hand-written routes it replaces.
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md): what
  is not built yet, and the argument for the order.

## Optional

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/AGENTS.md):
  instructions for agents working *on* Pelican — layering, comment rules, the
  testing order, the six build gates. Not needed to use the library.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
- [TODO](https://github.com/matthewjones372/pelican/blob/main/TODO.md): which HTTP
  libraries are planned next, on the server and client side.
